Q3 deliveries 486,532: Model 3/Y +10.5k, other models -4.1k (S/X discontinued), so auto revenue is roughly flat to slightly up. calls.reasoning: Q3 2026 has closed and the deliveries are known: 486,532 total (478,237 Model 3/Y, 8,295 other models). Q2 2026 car sales of $20.0B imply about $40.8k per Model 3/Y if the other models average about $75k, which gives Q3 car sales of about $20.13B. Credits and leasing add about $0.5B. Energy is about $3.2B on 13.7 GWh. Services and other is $4.3-4.7B; Q2's unexplained +$0.84B jump may partly revert. The total is about $28.45B, with downside from mix and discounting during the inventory drawdown. Published revenue consensus is $27.7-28.3B and probably set before the delivery beat. No human market was found: the runs report Kalshi lists only delivery contracts, and Polymarket and Manifold have none.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on all the core facts: Q2 segment revenue, Q3 deliveries and mix, and storage deployed. The earnings-date dispute (Oct 21 vs Oct 28) does not matter for resolution. The consensus figures ($27.73B, $27.91B, $28.27B) cannot be checked without web access, so they serve only as a soft lower anchor, and most likely predate the delivery beat. The main judgment call is whether services and other holds its Q2 jump to $4.58B. The runs carried it flat or higher; I allow partial reversion and some ASP pressure from mix and inventory clearance. That puts my median at $28.45B, slightly below the runs' $28.5-28.7B. I carry forward Run 3's small 1% tail escapes on each side.
